source.title: OFFSIDE: Benchmarking Unlearning Misinformation in Multimodal Large Language Models
source.authors: Hao Zheng; Zi-Rui Pang; Ling Li; Zhi-Jie Deng; Yuhan Pu; Zhao-Wei Zhu; Xiaobo Xia; Jia-Heng Wei

record.tranche_reason: Tests recovery of unlearned information in MLLMs using corrective relearning and a prompt-based classification task, rather than the original studies' methods and measures.
record.gate_note: The study reports results from corrective relearning and classification when rumor information is included in the prompt. These directly bear on recovery. The statement that all methods failed to unlearn visual rumors is also recorded as an aggregate result. Values used to select training settings are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study applies five standard unlearning methods (GA, GD, KL, PO, NPO) to Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B on a new multimodal rumor benchmark. It reports whether forgotten rumors persist under multiple-choice elicitation and return after fine-tuning on related corrected data. That is a new setting (MLLMs, real images) with direct results on versions A, B and E.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that baselines remain vulnerable to prompt-based (classification) retrieval and that unlearned rumors bounce back after simple relearning, so methods conceal rather than remove the rumors. They also conclude that all methods fail on visual rumors, that unimodal methods fail on multimodal rumors, and that unlearning efficacy is largely driven by catastrophic forgetting.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates GA, GD, KL minimization, PO, and NPO on manually curated multimodal football-rumor data using classification and corrective relearning; it does not reproduce the original sources' setups.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model size and unlearning method; 7B GD classification accuracy is a marked exception to the high values of the other methods. Relearning outcomes also vary across method-model pairs.

fits_no_version.finding: No method unlearned visual rumors embedded in images. The authors attribute this to the model reading the image without correct knowledge to override it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning stored rumors does not stop an MLLM from repeating misinformation present in the input image.

fits_no_version.finding: Sample IDs forgotten by GA/GD/KL/NPO overlap 71%/48%/58%/60% with IDs forgotten by vanilla after simple relearning (catastrophic forgetting).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Which items baseline unlearning removes resembles catastrophic forgetting from continual fine-tuning.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The authors note that each player has only 8 QA pairs and only one is a visual rumor, and that they do not propose a new unlearning algorithm. Relearning results are for corrected versions of the same rumors, not unrelated or loosely related examples. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

untested.parts: Only GA, GD, KL, PO and NPO with LoRA on Qwen2.5-VL are tested. No RMU, ELM or WMDP-style hazardous knowledge. General ability (MM-Bench) is a selection filter, not an outcome.

Relearning uses corrected true data about the same players only. No unrelated or loosely related data, and no relearning on a subset of the forgotten rumors themselves. No retrain-from-scratch control after relearning.
Entire version: no activation ablation or interpretability analysis (listed as future work).
Only multiple-choice elicitation with the rumor among the options. No rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages or in-context few-shot attacks.
Entire version: no new robust method is proposed or tested.

missing.what: Forget-set MCQ accuracy after relearning: 7B GA 57.5, GD 62.2, KL 63.8, PO 64.7, NPO 59.3 vs vanilla-relearned 59.7. 3B values 46.9-51.3 vs 53.2. GD 7B goes from 23.5% to 62.2%.
Forget-set generation and fact scores after unlearning (e.g., KL 7B fact 0.57, PO 1.59) and pretrained references, needed to judge whether generation was suppressed.
Fine-grained unlearning (3B): private-info MCQ rises above vanilla (57.2-59.6% vs 56.5%) while shared info also degrades.
Text-only (unimodal) unlearning fails to remove rumors when queried with images; numbers only in the figure.

record.verdict_notes: Rows r1-r10 carry one state for both A and E. The state describes MCQ retention, so 'observed' means A fails and E holds. Results are reported only for runs whose MM-Bench score was not degraded, which is a selection step. For B, the forget-set fact score mixes rumor QAs with shared player facts (height, birthdate) that the relearn set also teaches. Rising scores may therefore reflect relearned shared facts rather than rumor recovery, and no retrain-from-scratch control after relearning is shown. The vanilla-relearned scores (r12, r13) are the apt comparator. No uncertainty estimates; LoRA only; two models from one family.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests five baselines on its MLLM rumor benchmark, not every unlearning method in the claim. It does not test recovery through activation edits, quantization, prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or unrelated examples.
Relearning uses corrected information about the same rumors; the study does not test unrelated or loosely related examples, or an arbitrary small subset of forgotten facts.
No activation-direction ablation or internal-access-versus-deletion analysis is reported.
No weight quantization attack is reported.
The study tests classification with rumor information in the prompt. It does not test rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information as separate attack conditions.
The study evaluates existing baselines and does not test a newer method designed to resist the listed attacks.
